text:
Marathon's stock rose modestly today as it recovered from a significant dip earlier this week, with the gain driven by a combination of strong refinery utilization and elevated heating oil prices. US refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, near maximum, and heating oil prices have spiked 59% from last winter—a jump that typically benefits refiners who produce these fuels and can sell them at higher margins. The stock has climbed $42 over the past week as these tailwinds have built confidence in the refining sector.

That said, the longer view shows headwinds: the stock is still down 6.76% over two weeks, and recent news suggests oil markets may be shifting toward oversupply. Russian crude production has rebounded and global supply is now exceeding demand, which can pressure oil prices and refining margins over time. While today's bounce reflects near-term strength in the refining environment, that underlying supply surplus could weigh on the sector if it persists.
